title: RunFlow Gateway: idempotent operator shortcut bridge for safe, replayable admin scripts
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Summary:
Implement a lightweight gateway ( RunFlow ) that converts ad-hoc operator scripts and CLI shortcuts into first-class, idempotent runbook tasks. The gateway should enable safe dry-runs, strong auditability, permission checks, and fast replay while preserving existing one-off shell ergonomics used by support/SRE.

Goals:
- Provide a developer-friendly shim so engineers can continue using familiar short scripts but have executions recorded as structured tasks in the runbook system.
- Make multi-step remediation transactional or guided (two-phase apply + confirm) to reduce blast radius on complex fixes.
- Ensure auditing, RBAC enforcement, and per-execution telemetry appear in the Console tracing and event timeline.
- Support a dry-run simulation mode that produces an execution plan and side-effect-free samples for reviewers.

Non-goals:
- Not intended to replace the full runbook DSL; this is an ergonomic bridge for common short workflows (5-8 steps).
- Not an access control replacement for customer-managed KMS or vaults.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Convert and run at least 12 common operator scripts from the SRE cookbook as idempotent RunFlow tasks with preserved semantics.
2) Dry-run mode returns deterministic plan + simulated outputs for >=95% of scripts in the sample set.
3) Every execution is stored as a structured event with requestor, git-commit of the task template, parameter diffs, and a trace link visible in Console.
4) Apply path must support an opt-in two-phase confirm flow with an explicit human confirmation step.
5) Latency: gateway dispatch overhead < 250ms P95 for small tasks.
6) Telemetry: count of runs, failures, dry-runs, replays, and average duration emitted to existing runbook metrics.

Design notes / approach:
- A shallow parser that recognizes a curated subset of shell idioms and maps them to primitive tasklets (api-call, exec-safe, db-migration-check, restart-service).
- A thin runtime wrapper that enforces idempotency by adding guarded checks (resource-state precondition) and replay tokens.
- Two execution modes: dry-run (simulate + plan) and apply (transactional sequence with optional confirm).
- Integrate with the existing runbook datastore: each RunFlow invocation becomes a runbook instance with typed steps and inputs.
- Implement RBAC checks by delegating to the existing identity service; escalate to manual approval when elevated scopes are required.
- Web and Slack UI components: quick preview for dry-run results and a one-click approval action.

Telemetry and observability:
- Emit structured events to the runbook timeline and tracer with span tags: runflow.template, runflow.mode, runflow.result.
- Add Console view with ability to filter by originating script hash and operator identity.

Security and safety considerations:
- Default to dry-run for any unrecognized idiom; operator must explicitly opt-in to apply.
- Rate-limit apply-mode per-operator to avoid accidental cascades.
- All apply runs must record an allowlist check against the org policy (e.g., no direct RDS deletes without 2 approvals).
- Security review required before public rollout.

Migration path and rollout:
- Phase 0 (internal prototype): convert 5 high-value scripts and validate simulation fidelity with SRE.
- Phase 1 (beta): enable opt-in for SRE and oncall for two teams; collect metrics and failure modes.
- Phase 2 (team self-serve): expand catalog and expose RunFlow CLI shim; add Slack approval integration.
- Phase 3 (org-wide): enable RBAC controls and enable default dry-run policy with training docs.

Deliverables / tasks:
- Parser & mapping table for idioms (ENG-604322).
- Runtime wrapper and idempotency helpers (ENG-604323).
- Console timeline + filter view (PM & FE pairing) (ENG-604324).
- Slack approver shortcut and webhook integration (ENG-604325).
- Docs + playbook for SRE on supported scripts + training session (ENG-604326).

Dependencies:
- Identity/RBAC APIs must support per-action policy introspection.
- Runbook datastore schema changes to accept 'origin_script' and 'dry_run_plan' fields.
- Telemetry pipeline capacity for additional event volume.

Open questions:
- How far should the parser go? We should start conservative and expand based on measured operator patterns.
- Do we support parameterized templates stored in git or only inline ephemeral tasks?

comments: 2026-03-02 - Avery Chen: Kickoff meeting with SRE product owners. Collected 18 candidate scripts; prioritized 12 for phase 0. Agreed to start conservative parser that maps to 7 primitive tasklets.

2026-03-05 - Marcus Patel: Prototype runtime created. Dry-run simulation works for 4 of the initial scripts; two failed due to unhandled sed/awk piping idioms. Added plan to sanitize and reject complex pipelines with guidance.
2026-03-07 - Design review (Priya Rao): UX for dry-run preview needs clearer failure states and explicit ‘what will change’ diff. Added low-fi mock for Console timeline and Slack modal.
2026-03-09 - Security (Jordan Kim): Flagged need for policy allowlist for destructive commands and requirement for 2-approver flow on DB deletions. Security review requested before beta rollout.

2026-03-10 - Marcus Patel: Integration test harness added. End-to-end dry-run for 10 sample scripts now passing in CI; two scripts still require manual transform. Next: implement confirmation modal and audit enrichment.
